layers.name: Land fraction

explanation.what: The share of each cell that is land. It is the background map for this case.
explanation.measures: Fraction of the cell, from 0 to 1.
explanation.inspect: Use it to find your way around.

layers.attribution: W. B. Rossow, City College of New York NOAA/CREST. LANDMET L3 v1, DOI 10.5067/MEASURES/LANDMET/DATA001
limitations: A test dataset. It is not NISAR data and says nothing about the 2026 Rasuwa event: it is from 2007.
Cells are about 110 km across, so one cell can blend very different terrain, especially in mountains.

layers.name: Land surface skin temperature

explanation.what: How hot the ground surface was, from the ISCCP FD satellite product.
explanation.measures: Temperature of the surface itself, in kelvin. It swings far more than air temperature.
explanation.inspect: Move through the day: the warm peak should travel from east to west with local noon.
explanation.establishes: Surface temperature only, at about 110 km scale.

layers.attribution: W. B. Rossow, City College of New York NOAA/CREST. LANDMET L3 v1, DOI 10.5067/MEASURES/LANDMET/DATA001
limitations: A test dataset. It is not NISAR data and says nothing about the 2026 Rasuwa event: it is from 2007.
Cells are about 110 km across, so one cell can blend very different terrain, especially in mountains.

layers.name: Near-surface air temperature

explanation.what: Air temperature about 2 m above ground, retrieved from satellite sounders (ISCCP NNHIRS).
explanation.inspect: Compare it with skin temperature, and with the station temperature layer.
explanation.establishes: A satellite retrieval at about 110 km scale, not a station reading.

layers.attribution: W. B. Rossow, City College of New York NOAA/CREST. LANDMET L3 v1, DOI 10.5067/MEASURES/LANDMET/DATA001
limitations: A test dataset. It is not NISAR data and says nothing about the 2026 Rasuwa event: it is from 2007.
Cells are about 110 km across, so one cell can blend very different terrain, especially in mountains.

layers.name: Station air temperature

explanation.what: Air temperature from ground stations (Integrated Surface Database), gridded to the cells.
explanation.inspect: Compare it with the satellite air temperature. Sparse regions rely on filled values.
explanation.establishes: A gridded station product. Many cells hold filled rather than observed values.

layers.attribution: W. B. Rossow, City College of New York NOAA/CREST. LANDMET L3 v1, DOI 10.5067/MEASURES/LANDMET/DATA001
limitations: A test dataset. It is not NISAR data and says nothing about the 2026 Rasuwa event: it is from 2007.
Cells are about 110 km across, so one cell can blend very different terrain, especially in mountains.
Cells without nearby stations hold filled values.

layers.name: Surface pressure

explanation.what: Atmospheric pressure at the land surface (ISCCP NNHIRS).
explanation.measures: Pressure in hectopascals. It mostly follows terrain height.
explanation.inspect: High ground shows clearly as low pressure.
explanation.establishes: Mostly a map of elevation in this one-day view.

layers.attribution: W. B. Rossow, City College of New York NOAA/CREST. LANDMET L3 v1, DOI 10.5067/MEASURES/LANDMET/DATA001
limitations: A test dataset. It is not NISAR data and says nothing about the 2026 Rasuwa event: it is from 2007.
Cells are about 110 km across, so one cell can blend very different terrain, especially in mountains.

layers.name: Near-surface relative humidity

explanation.what: Relative humidity near the surface, retrieved from satellite sounders (ISCCP NNHIRS).
explanation.inspect: Values over 100 percent are retrieval artefacts, and are flagged as masked.
explanation.establishes: A satellite retrieval. It is not a station measurement.

layers.attribution: W. B. Rossow, City College of New York NOAA/CREST. LANDMET L3 v1, DOI 10.5067/MEASURES/LANDMET/DATA001
limitations: A test dataset. It is not NISAR data and says nothing about the 2026 Rasuwa event: it is from 2007.
Cells are about 110 km across, so one cell can blend very different terrain, especially in mountains.
The file allows values up to 150 percent. Those over 100 are flagged as masked.

layers.name: Station wind speed

explanation.what: Wind speed from ground stations (Integrated Surface Database).
explanation.measures: Wind speed in metres per second.
explanation.inspect: Check any extreme value: station records contain errors.
explanation.establishes: A gridded station product, sparse in many regions.

layers.attribution: W. B. Rossow, City College of New York NOAA/CREST. LANDMET L3 v1, DOI 10.5067/MEASURES/LANDMET/DATA001
limitations: A test dataset. It is not NISAR data and says nothing about the 2026 Rasuwa event: it is from 2007.
Cells are about 110 km across, so one cell can blend very different terrain, especially in mountains.
The file contains values up to 118.6 m/s. Anything above 60 m/s is treated as implausible and flagged as masked.

layers.name: Precipitation rate

explanation.what: Rain and snow rate from the merged TMPA and GPCP satellite records.
explanation.inspect: Most cells are dry on any given step.
explanation.establishes: Satellite precipitation at about 110 km scale.

layers.attribution: W. B. Rossow, City College of New York NOAA/CREST. LANDMET L3 v1, DOI 10.5067/MEASURES/LANDMET/DATA001
limitations: A test dataset. It is not NISAR data and says nothing about the 2026 Rasuwa event: it is from 2007.
Cells are about 110 km across, so one cell can blend very different terrain, especially in mountains.

layers.name: Snow cover fraction

explanation.what: The share of each cell covered by snow, for the whole day.
explanation.measures: Fraction of the cell, from 0 to 1.
explanation.inspect: Late December: the northern continents should be largely covered.
explanation.establishes: Snow cover only, for one day.

layers.attribution: W. B. Rossow, City College of New York NOAA/CREST. LANDMET L3 v1, DOI 10.5067/MEASURES/LANDMET/DATA001
limitations: A test dataset. It is not NISAR data and says nothing about the 2026 Rasuwa event: it is from 2007.

layers.name: Soil moisture

explanation.what: Water held in the top soil layer, from satellite retrievals, for the whole day.
explanation.inspect: Frozen and snow-covered ground usually has no retrieval.
explanation.establishes: Top-layer soil moisture only, with large gaps.

layers.attribution: W. B. Rossow, City College of New York NOAA/CREST. LANDMET L3 v1, DOI 10.5067/MEASURES/LANDMET/DATA001
limitations: A test dataset. It is not NISAR data and says nothing about the 2026 Rasuwa event: it is from 2007.

layers.name: Temporary flood fraction

explanation.what: The share of each cell temporarily flooded, for the whole day.
explanation.measures: Fraction of the cell, from 0 to 1.
explanation.establishes: A coarse estimate. It has nothing to do with the Rasuwa flood.

layers.attribution: W. B. Rossow, City College of New York NOAA/CREST. LANDMET L3 v1, DOI 10.5067/MEASURES/LANDMET/DATA001
limitations: A test dataset. It is not NISAR data and says nothing about the 2026 Rasuwa event: it is from 2007.

layers.name: Mean terrain height

explanation.what: Mean height of each cell, from ISCCP topography.
explanation.measures: Height above sea level in metres.
explanation.inspect: Note how much the Himalaya is smoothed at this scale.
explanation.establishes: Cell averages, far coarser than the 30 m terrain in the Rasuwa case.
